title: Decoding Intent from Fragments: Structure-Aware Late Interaction for Concept-Level EEG-to-Text Retrieval

problem.claim: EEG-to-text retrieval methods struggle to capture sparse, fragmented conceptual intents from continuous EEG signals.

gap.claim: Existing methods typically compress continuous EEG signals into holistic vectors, limiting granularity for discrete conceptual units.

contributions.claim: Introduces Brain Concept-to-Sentence Retrieval, a task for decoding intent from fragmented EEG signals.
Proposes SparkRetriever, a structure-aware retrieval model for aligning discrete EEG concepts with natural-language sentences.

Uses fine-grained late interaction, independent EEG semantic anchors, multi-positive contrastive learning, and subject embeddings to support multi-to-multi matching and address cross-subject variability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Brain Concept-to-Sentence Retrieval as a novel task.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the ZuCo benchmark, the authors report that SparkRetriever significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, with relative improvements of 23.4% to 33.7% across multiple metrics.
The authors report that multi-positive supervision is the primary driver of performance and mitigates bias from single-sentence alignment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Retrieval-based EEG-to-text decoding has emerged as an alternative to generative approaches, but existing methods use holistic EEG representations.
Holistic compression fails to capture sparse, fragmented conceptual intents in real-world brain-computer interaction.
The paper introduces BCSR and SparkRetriever, combining structure-aware late interaction with semantic anchors, multi-positive contrastive learning, and subject embeddings.
Experiments on ZuCo report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with multi-positive supervision identified as the main performance driver.

source_observation.claim: Preserving fragmented EEG concepts as independent semantic anchors enables fine-grained multi-to-multi matching with text tokens.

interpretation.claim: When the input contains sparse conceptual evidence, retaining local units may preserve retrieval-relevant structure better than holistic compression.

application.claim: Use late interaction or another token-level matching strategy for retrieval tasks involving fragmented signals or sparse intent representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond EEG-to-text retrieval or the ZuCo benchmark.

source_observation.claim: Multi-positive supervision is reported to mitigate bias inherent in single-sentence alignment.

interpretation.claim: Training with multiple valid positive alignments may better represent ambiguous or fragmented semantic correspondence.

application.claim: Consider multi-positive contrastive objectives when one input can correspond to multiple semantically valid targets.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how positives are constructed or when multi-positive supervision may be ineffective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset size, subject count, preprocessing, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablations, statistical significance, or error analysis.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvements.
